Industry sources say Airbus has toyed with using an engine from GE Aerospace for the roughly 400-seat A350-2000, but that the engine maker has so far shown limited interest in joining. Wagner reiterated that Airbus was confident of reaching its year-end delivery goals despite recent industrial quality flaws. Longer term, Airbus continues to look at a "notional" date of 2030 for launching an all-new single-aisle jet, he said.

item.title: Container ship sinks near Hormuz after being hit by projectile
item.description: A Singapore-flagged container ship has sunk near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by a projectile, while a dry bulk carrier damaged in an earlier attack is also reported to be sinking, maritime security sources said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Saul, Renee Maltezou
item.content:encoded: A Singapore-flagged container ship has sunk near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by a projectile, while a dry bulk carrier damaged in an earlier attack is also reported to be sinking, maritime security sources said on Wednesday. Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days. The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride, a small container vessel with capacity for 2,824 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU), sank while sailing through the strait, the sources said. "GFS PRIDE sustained damage and a fire on board, and has since sunk. All 21 crew members were safely evacuated. No injuries have been reported," the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said in a statement on Wednesday, adding that the vessel had been sailing through the strait on Tuesday. The loss of the GFS Pride marks the second vessel to sink since the US-Iran war began on February 28, according to data from the UN shipping agency, the International Maritime Organization. "MPA is deeply concerned about the continued attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz," the Singapore authority said. "Such attacks are unprovoked, unjustifiable, and a breach of international law." GFS Pride's United Arab Emirates-based manager, GFS Ship Management FZE, could not be immediately reached for comment. The latest incident comes amid a sharp escalation in threats to commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade passed before the war. Tehran has sought to tighten its grip on the waterway since U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, restricting transit in an effort to gain leverage over Washington. The United States, meanwhile, has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and expanded sanctions to intensify economic pressure on Tehran. Iran is increasingly deploying new tactics against vessels transiting the strait as it seeks to keep oil prices elevated and influence US midterm elections, [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"two senior Iranian officials told Reuters."] While Iran and the US have focused their attacks on tankers, cargo and container vessels have also been attacked, immobilised or sunk. In a separate incident, the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged Cape Dao was reported to be sinking close to the strait after being struck by a projectile on September 23, the maritime security sources said. "The Antigua & Barbuda flagged bulk carrier CAPE DAO, originally hit on the 23 September, is reported to be sinking after an unsuccessful rescue attempt," British maritime risk management group Vanguard said in a note on Wednesday. The vessel's UAE-based manager Peonies Shipmanagement FZE could not be immediately reached for comment. The Maltese-flagged container ship Safeen Prestige was hit by a projectile in March and later sank north of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guards attacked and seized the container ship MSC Francesca in April.

item.title: Fed rate hike call seen tight as inflation heats up
item.description: A Federal Reserve interest-rate decision later this month may be a closer call than previously thought after Labor Department data showed consumer prices were up 3.7% last month from a year earlier, well above the Fed's 2% target and moving in the wrong direction.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: A Federal Reserve interest-rate decision later this month may be a closer call than previously thought after Labor Department data showed consumer prices were up 3.7% last month from a year earlier, well above the Fed's 2% target and moving in the wrong direction. Higher gasoline prices from the Middle East war were a main driver. Excluding volatile food and energy prices, the core Consumer Price Index (CPI) was up 2.6%, more than the 2.5% economists polled by Reuters had projected. The Fed lifted the policy rate in September to a target range of 3.75%-4.00% to bring down too-high inflation, and officials have said they are looking closely for signs of broadening price pressures that could keep inflation high even if gas prices fall, necessitating more policy tightening. Wednesday's data contained plenty of such signs. "The surprise was not concentrated in any one item, like it was with wireless in the August report, but instead reflected a number of components showing strength, i.e., it was broad-based," wrote Omair Sharif, founder of Inflation Insights. Software prices were up 28% from a year earlier, the largest increase ever, and toy prices also notched a record rise, the data showed -- emblematic of inflationary impulses from both AI-driven demand and higher tariffs under the Trump administration. "This means that inflation is broadening out, something that is not a good omen for the Fed and would raise the probability for an increase in rates at the end of the October FOMC meeting," wrote Raymond James Chief Economist Eugenio Aleman, referring to the Fed's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee, which next meets October 27-28. In recent weeks several of the Fed's most influential policymakers have signaled there's time to weigh more data before delivering what most believe will be at least one more rate hike by year's end, and traders had bet heavily against a second straight hike under Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh -- especially just a week before November elections that will decide if Trump's Republican party holds on to majorities in Congress. After Wednesday's economic data, interest-rate futures are priced for around even odds of an October rate hike, a place of unusual uncertainty around the outcome of a Fed decision just two weeks away. Fed policymakers are also weighing the risk of tightening too fast and unduly slowing the labor market. Unemployment has been low, but job gains have also cooled. "September CPI keeps inflation concerns alive, with core inflation still sticky, but weaker jobs data and fragile consumer sentiment mean the Fed still has room to hold in October," PPHC Chief Economist Martin Beck said.

item.title: Morgan Stanley übertrifft Gewinnerwartungen dank Aktienhandel
item.description: Die US-Investmentbank Morgan Stanley hat im dritten Quartal dank eines starken Aktienhandels mehr verdient als erwartet. Das auf die Aktionäre entfallende Ergebnis stieg um 6,5 Prozent auf 4,91 Milliarden Dollar oder 3,03 Dollar je Aktie, wie das Institut am Mittwoch mitteilte. Analysten hatten laut Daten des Anbieters LSEG lediglich mit einem Gewinn von 2,91 Dollar je Aktie gerechnet. Die Nettoerträge kletterten um 11,6 Prozent auf 20,34 Milliarden Dollar.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die US-Investmentbank Morgan Stanley (MS.N) hat im dritten Quartal dank eines starken Aktienhandels mehr verdient als erwartet. Das auf die Aktionäre entfallende Ergebnis stieg um 6,5 Prozent auf 4,91 Milliarden Dollar oder 3,03 Dollar je Aktie, wie das Institut am Mittwoch mitteilte. Analysten hatten laut Daten des Anbieters LSEG lediglich mit einem Gewinn von 2,91 Dollar je Aktie gerechnet. Die Nettoerträge kletterten um 11,6 Prozent auf 20,34 Milliarden Dollar. Morgan Stanley profitierte von der hohen Volatilität an den Finanzmärkten. Auslöser der Kursschwankungen waren die Zinsentscheidung der US-Notenbank Fed sowie der Krieg zwischen den USA und dem Iran, die Anleger zu Umschichtungen ihrer Portfolios veranlassten. Bereits am [USN:L8N45Z1C1 TEXT:"Dienstag"] hatten einige andere Banken ein ähnliches Bild gezeichnet. Während Goldman Sachs (GS.N) und die Citigroup (C.N) ihre Gewinne unerwartet deutlich steigerten, verfehlte jedoch der Branchenprimus JPMorgan (JPM.N) wegen eines schwächeren Investmentbankings die Erwartungen. Wells Fargo (WFC.N) übertraf zwar die Gewinnziele, enttäuschte Anleger jedoch bei den Erträgen und dem Zinsüberschuss. Die Bank of America (BAC.N) berichtete am [USN:L8N4601CK TEXT:"Mittwoch"] von einem Gewinneinbruch infolge eines schwachen Kapitalmarktgeschäfts und einer Milliardenstrafe. Bei Morgan Stanley war Treiber der Entwicklung der Aktienhandel, dessen Einnahmen um fast 41 Prozent auf 5,8 Milliarden Dollar in die Höhe schnellten. Im Anleihehandel verzeichnete Morgan Stanley hingegen einen Rückgang der Erträge um 7,3 Prozent auf 2,01 Milliarden Dollar. VERMÖGENSVERWALTUNG UNTER ERWARTUNGEN Im wichtigen Geschäft mit der Vermögensverwaltung stiegen die Einnahmen zwar um 10,1 Prozent auf 9,07 Milliarden Dollar, blieben damit aber leicht unter den Erwartungen. "Das ist bedeutsam, da die Vermögensverwaltung einer der wichtigsten strategischen Wachstumsmotoren der Bank ist", erklärte Marktexperte Daniel Coatsworth vom Broker AJ Bell. Morgan Stanley hatte den Bereich in den vergangenen Jahren ausgebaut, um die Abhängigkeit vom schwankungsanfälligen Investmentbanking und dem Handel zu verringern. Das Investmentbanking behauptete sich in einem schwierigen Umfeld. Obwohl das weltweite Volumen von Fusionen und Übernahmen gegenüber dem Vorquartal um 41 Prozent einbrach und der Markt für Börsengänge gedämpft blieb, legten die Erträge der Sparte um zwei Prozent auf 2,16 Milliarden Dollar zu. Morgan Stanley agierte unter anderem als führender Finanzberater beim Kauf des deutschen Lieferdienstes Delivery Hero (DHER.DE) durch Uber (UBER.N) für 14,8 Milliarden Dollar. Zudem sicherte sich das Institut bei den erwarteten Börsengängen der Firmen für Künstliche Intelligenz (KI), Anthropic und OpenAI, Plätze in den Bankenkonsortien. Dagegen sanken die Nettoerträge in der Investment-Management-Sparte, in der auch die Privatkreditfonds gebündelt sind, auf 1,46 Milliarden Dollar nach 1,65 Milliarden vor Jahresfrist. Vor dem Hintergrund von Befürchtungen, dass KI-Technologie Softwareunternehmen in den Portfolios schaden könnte, verlangten Anleger Gelder aus einem wichtigen Fonds zurück.

item.title: Le Portugal choisit Lufthansa, et non Air France-KLM, pour prendre 44,9% de TAP
item.description: Le gouvernement portugais a annoncé mercredi avoir choisi Lufthansa pour acquérir une participation de 44,9% dans la compagnie TAP Air Portugal, pour 1,2 milliard d'euros, Lisbonne préférant ainsi la compagnie allemande à Air France-KLM , qui avait également soumis une offre.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le gouvernement portugais a annoncé mercredi avoir choisi Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) pour acquérir une participation de 44,9% dans la compagnie TAP Air Portugal, pour 1,2 milliard d'euros, Lisbonne préférant ainsi la compagnie allemande à Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) , qui avait également soumis une offre. Cet accord, qui a mis des années à se concrétiser et qui a été reporté à plusieurs reprises, constitue une nouvelle étape dans la consolidation du secteur aérien européen, un processus jugé nécessaire pour aider les petites compagnies nationales à gagner en résilience au sein de groupes plus importants. Selon les analystes et les dirigeants du secteur, cette consolidation devrait s'accélérer, la flambée des prix du kérosène, liée à la guerre en Iran, contraignant les compagnies aériennes les plus fragiles à s'associer à des groupes plus importants et mieux capitalisés. Lufthansa, qui détient déjà Austrian Airlines, ITA Airways et SWISS, et Air France-KLM avaient soumis fin septembre des offres finales revues à la hausse . Le Premier ministre portugais Luis Montenegro a déclaré lors d'une conférence de presse que l'offre retenue dépassait de 16% celle d’Air France-KLM. "Bien que le groupe (Air France-KLM) soit naturellement déçu de ne pas avoir été retenu, il se félicite du dialogue constructif qui a eu lieu tout au long du processus", a dit un porte-parole d’Air France-KLM à Reuters. S'exprimant lors du World Aviation Festival à Lisbonne avant l'annonce, le directeur général de TAP, Luis Rodrigues, a déclaré que rejoindre un groupe plus important permettrait à la compagnie portugaise "d'accéder à un plus grand nombre de ressources à un meilleur rapport qualité-prix". Le gouvernement portugais a précisé que sa décision reposait non seulement sur le prix, mais aussi sur le plan industriel de chaque soumissionnaire pour TAP - y compris sa stratégie en matière de croissance et de viabilité à long terme de la compagnie aérienne. Le principal atout de TAP réside dans ses liaisons reliant Lisbonne au Brésil, à l'Afrique lusophone et aux États-Unis. En juin, TAP exploitait une flotte de 101 appareils desservant 93 destinations à travers le monde. La compagnie aérienne a transporté un nombre record de 8,2 millions de passagers au premier semestre 2026, en hausse de 4,2% par rapport à l'année précédente.

item.title: Ukraine says SpaceX hampers drones for attack and defence, as US ties fray
item.description: Ukraine said Elon Musk's SpaceX had limited Starlink services on Wednesday, hampering Ukrainian drones for attack missions and air defences, as relations between Kyiv and Washington have taken a sharp turn for the worse.
item.dc:creator: Yuliia Dysa, Dan Peleschuk
item.content:encoded: Ukraine said Elon Musk's SpaceX had limited Starlink services on Wednesday, hampering Ukrainian drones for attack missions and air defences, as relations between Kyiv and Washington have taken a sharp turn for the worse. Russia rained more missiles and drones down on Ukrainian cities, knocking out electricity for hundreds of thousands of people in attacks President Volodymyr Zelenskiy called "ostentatious disrespect" to Donald Trump's call for an energy ceasefire. The US president publicly turned on Zelenskiy in recent days after abruptly lifting sanctions on Russian diesel last week, under political pressure to lower fuel prices that have soared since he launched a war against Iran. He has called on Kyiv to halt attacks on Russian refineries, and said Ukrainians should replace their wartime leader. Trump announced at the weekend that Ukraine and Russia both agreed to halt attacks on energy targets, although neither side confirmed this and the past two days have seen intensive Russian bombing, including of Ukrainian power stations. After a night of bombardment of the capital Kyiv, Russian strikes continued throughout the day on Wednesday with six people killed in the western city of Lutsk, where the regional governor said a warehouse and a residential building were hit. Ukraine, for its part, continued long-range strikes on Russia, hitting [USN:L8N46009S TEXT:"Russia's biggest data centre"], although it says it is holding back from hitting energy targets for now to show respect for Trump. NO WARNING BEFORE STARLINK CUTS Ukrainian military officials said Musk's SpaceX (SPCX.O) had without warning interrupted functioning of military-grade Starlink terminals when they are moving at high speed. Kyiv installs Starlink receptors in many of its drones as part of their onboard guidance systems. Starlink operates across Ukraine, including in territory held by Russian forces. "Our defence forces did not receive a warning about this limitation, and this led to the disruption of several missions," presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram. The speed cutoff hampers Ukraine's ability to conduct strikes on Russian targets inside Ukraine, and to defend itself from Russian drones using its own interceptor drones, according to a defence ministry source and another military source. Beskrestnov said SpaceX had imposed a speed limit of 160 km per hour. The defence ministry source told Reuters military units had reported guidance systems losing their connections at speeds of less than half that. SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The defence ministry source said Ukraine was in contact with the company as well as the US government and NATO to seek clarification over the sudden limitations. The suggestion that Musk's company had limited Ukrainian military capabilities drew a sharp response from Poland, which pays for Ukrainian Starlink subscriptions on Kyiv's behalf. "Hey, @elonmusk, big man, are you playing politics with your products again?" Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski asked Musk on X. "As your European customers, we are watching you." There was no immediate response from Musk, who in the past has called Sikorski a "small man". Shares in European satellite operator Eutelsat (ETL.PA) , which is seen as Europe's best shot at taking on Starlink, [USN:L6N4600QK TEXT:"jumped on Wednesday"] as some investors bet that European providers could benefit from growing strains between Washington and Kyiv. Musk is a close political ally of Trump, and the suggestion that SpaceX might limit Ukrainian capabilities reinforced wider Ukrainian concerns that Washington could withhold battlefield support to compel its one-time ally to make concessions. Sources have told Reuters and other media that the US has threatened to cut off intelligence for early warning of missile strikes on Ukraine, to press Kyiv to suspend attacks on Russian oil refineries. NO WARNING AHEAD OF MISSILES Rescue workers in Kyiv were stretchering the injured from the wreckage of a blasted-out residential building overnight, while firefighters battled a huge blaze in the darkness. Officials said 2 people were killed and 21 wounded at the site. Some 600,000 people were left without power as Russian missiles careened into power stations during hours of attacks that primarily targeted Kyiv and Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city. Russia's defence ministry confirmed it had struck four power plants in and around Kyiv and two in Kharkiv, among other targets. Zelenskiy said 30 energy facilities were damaged. Ukrainian officials said late on Tuesday they had received no warnings from Western partners for a second day before Russian missiles hit the capital. Trump had insisted on Tuesday that Washington was [USN:L1N45Z0GP TEXT:"still sharing intelligence"]. Zelenskiy cast the latest Russian attacks as a deliberate snub to Trump's declaration of a ceasefire on energy targets. "Russia does not consider the American President's statements strong," Zelenskiy wrote on X. "The strike was entirely deliberate and demonstrative in its scale – Russia has never before shown such ostentatious disrespect toward the United States." Zelenskiy has said Ukraine is willing to observe an energy ceasefire and has not targeted Russian refineries since Trump announced it, but will not continue to hold back if Russia ignores the purported truce. The Kremlin said on Tuesday that contacts were continuing about an energy truce. Ukraine reported downing just 4 out of 39 Russian missiles, reflecting Kyiv's weakened air-defences against fast-moving ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones amid a shortage of weapons.

item.title: Lufthansa wins race for €1.2 billion stake in Portuguese carrier TAP
item.description: Portugal's government on Wednesday picked Lufthansa to buy a stake of up to 49.9% in TAP Air Portugal for €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) over rival Air France-KLM , making the German airline the strategic partner of one of Europe's last unaligned flag carriers.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Joanna Plucinska
item.content:encoded: Portugal's government on Wednesday picked Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) to buy a stake of up to 49.9% in TAP Air Portugal for €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) over rival Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) , making the German airline the strategic partner of one of Europe's last unaligned flag carriers. The deal, years in the making and repeatedly delayed, is the next step in the [USN:L6N42E079 TEXT:"consolidation"] of Europe's airline industry, a process seen as necessary to help smaller national carriers become more resilient as part of larger groups. Analysts and industry executives say that is likely to accelerate as soaring jet fuel prices linked to the war in Iran force weaker airlines to work with larger, better-capitalised groups. Lufthansa, which already owns Austrian Airlines, ITA Airways and SWISS among other carriers, beat rival Air France-KLM after both airlines submitted improved final bids in late September. "This will give them an additional hub, albeit in a sphere of influence where they've lacked reach currently," said aviation analyst John Strickland, as Lufthansa will gain further access to Southwest Europe and other parts of the world by extension. TAP's main attraction is its valuable landing slots connecting Lisbon with Brazil, Portuguese-speaking Africa and the US, routes that underpin Portugal's diaspora ties, tourism flows and investment links. Prime Minister Luis Montenegro told a news briefing the winning bid exceeded Air France-KLM's offer by 16%. Speaking at the World Aviation Festival in Lisbon before the announcement, TAP CEO Luis Rodrigues said joining a larger group would allow the Portuguese carrier to "access a larger pool of resources at better value". THE PERKS The government said its decision was based not only on price but also on each bidder's industrial plan for TAP, including its strategy for the airline's growth and long-term sustainability. It wants TAP's partner to expand operations and connectivity across Portugal's airport network, not only at Lisbon's hub but also in Porto, Faro, the Azores and Madeira. Infrastructure Minister Miguel Pinto Luz said the Lufthansa Group has committed to increasing TAP's fleet to 117 aircraft by 2035 and 130 after 2035, when Lisbon's new airport is expected to be operational. As of June, TAP operated a fleet of 101 aircraft serving 93 destinations worldwide — 52 in Europe, 16 in South and Central America, 14 in Africa and 11 in North America. TAP carried a record 8.2 million passengers in the first half of 2026, up 4.2% from a year earlier, while operating revenue rose 4.3%. A ROCKY ROAD AHEAD Analysts pointed to Lufthansa's ongoing financial woes as a potential challenge in TAP's turnaround. Such deals require initial investment, and the pay-off isn't always guaranteed. "Lufthansa is still struggling financially. Lufthansa Deutsche Airlines, as the largest part of the group, is still losing money. It has to get its own house in order," Strickland told Reuters. Lufthansa has vowed to reach an operating profit of 8% to 10% between 2028 and 2030 and to simplify and centralise its operations in an effort to rebuild investor confidence. The turnaround of Italy's ITA is still ongoing, too, Strickland said, with investors and analysts previously worrying about the impact of Lufthansa's fragmented and spread-out network. (This story has been corrected to clarify that the plan is to expand TAP’s fleet to 117 aircraft, not by 117 aircraft, in paragraph 11.)

item.title: US bank regulator faults several large lenders over debanking practices
item.description: A top US bank regulator issued a report on Wednesday finding some of the country's largest banks unfairly denied services to some clients on political, religious or other grounds, but stopped short of imposing penalties.
item.dc:creator: Pete Schroeder, Manya Saini
item.content:encoded: A top US bank regulator issued a report on Wednesday finding some of the country's largest banks unfairly denied services to some clients on political, religious or other grounds, but stopped short of imposing penalties. The [USN:L4N4491DY TEXT:"debanking"] report from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency covered nine of the nation's largest banks by asset size. The regulator found each had policies restricting some clients' access to financial services based on subjective criteria rather than financial risk. Banks have said they close accounts or deny services because of legal, financial or reputational risks, not politics. The regulator criticized the banks for the practices, but did not indicate any sanctions or punishments were forthcoming. It said it may consider policy changes to discourage such activity. FAIR ACCESS IS A MANDATE: REGULATOR The review, which began in September 2025, scrutinized banks that collectively hold a majority of US commercial banking assets. "Americans should have access to financial services regardless of their beliefs, affiliations, or political views. Fair access to financial services is not a mantra — it is a mandate," Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan Gould said in a statement. After President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing a review of alleged debanking, [USN:L4N42C182 TEXT:"regulators and banks moved to eliminate the use of reputation risk "]in assessing clients, though[USN:L4N4491DY TEXT:" the issue remains contentious. "] Conservative politicians and business groups have accused banks of cutting off companies in sectors including fossil fuels, firearms and cryptocurrency , making debanking a flashpoint in Washington financial policy. Large banks have denied rejecting customers on political or religious grounds, arguing instead that years of aggressive regulatory pressure discouraged them from serving certain sectors and urging Washington to establish clearer rules on who they can and cannot serve. The OCC found that concerns about public opinion had led at least one bank to distance itself from certain customer affiliations that could be viewed as partisan. It added that banks generally lacked clear, measurable standards and objective, risk-based criteria for assessing reputational risks associated with customer relationships. "The OCC will continue to work with our regulatory partners to further assess the extent to which bank policies implementing money laundering and terrorist financing program requirements have contributed to debanking and will take appropriate action as needed," the report said. Earlier this year, Trump [USN:L4N3YN1QS TEXT:"filed a $5 billion lawsuit"] against JPMorgan Chase and its CEO Jamie Dimon, alleging the bank closed several of his accounts for political reasons. JPMorgan, the largest US bank, has denied closing accounts on political or religious grounds, and filed a motion to dismiss the lawsuit on Tuesday. A bank spokesperson said the lender prohibits political and religious discrimination, and added, "Years of operating in a regulatory environment that often second-guessed decisions contributed to a culture of caution across the banking industry. That system needs fixing." Trump has also [USN:S0N3OG012 TEXT:"accused other lenders"], including Bank of America (BAC.N) , the country's second-biggest lender by assets, of debanking him in early 2025. A Bank of America spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the new report. The bank has previously said it does not comment on client matters and would welcome clearer rules from bank regulators on how to conduct its activities.

item.title: BofA misses profit estimates on trading weakness, books $1.2 billion charge
item.description: Bank of America missed third-quarter profit estimates on Wednesday due to weakness in its trading business and disclosed a $1.2 billion charge tied to a regulatory penalty over failures to detect potential money-laundering activity.
item.dc:creator: Arasu Basil, Saeed Azhar
item.content:encoded: Bank of America (BAC.N) missed third-quarter profit estimates on Wednesday due to weakness in its trading business and disclosed a $1.2 billion charge tied to a regulatory penalty over failures to detect potential money-laundering activity. Shares of the second-biggest US lender fell more than 8%, hitting their lowest price since May. The Wall Street giant posted weaker fixed income, currency and commodities revenue, mirroring third-quarter trends at rivals [USN:L4N45Z10B TEXT:"JPMorgan Chase"] (JPM.N) , [USN:L4N45Z0VX TEXT:"Wells Fargo"] (WFC.N) and [USN:L4N45Z111 TEXT:"Goldman Sachs"] (GS.N) . "The poor capital markets performance doubles the negative impact of the earnings miss," Zacks Investment Management Chief Market Strategist Brian Mulberry said. BofA's sales and trading revenue fell 5% to $5.1 billion in the quarter, as weakness in FICC overshadowed record quarterly equities trading. The bank had last month projected quarterly sales and trading revenue to be relatively flat compared to last year. "Reduced client activity and changing market conditions, including a major shift in interest rates, significantly affected our leading FICC businesses, including credit mortgages and municipals," Chief Financial Officer Alastair Borthwick said. Rival JPMorgan on Tuesday also [USN:L4N45Z10B TEXT:"fell short"] of quarterly profit estimates as dealmaking, bond trading momentum slowed down. Asked how much longer he plans on remaining BofA's CEO, Brian Moynihan said succession is the board's decision. Moynihan has been at the helm of the storied US bank since 2010 and is one of the longest-serving CEOs of a major US bank. REGULATORY SETTLEMENT CHARGE The fine, [USN:L6N45Z18I TEXT:"unveiled late Tuesday"], stems from BofA's failure to report over $5 billion in suspicious activity to the US government. The actions, which include the third-largest penalty in US Treasury history, highlight [USN:L6N45U1B5 TEXT:"growing regulatory scrutiny"] of shortcomings in tackling money laundering at US financial giants. "There's no asset cap here. It won't crowd out anything," Borthwick told analysts. Regulators have placed BofA under a consent order — a major regulatory punishment — that requires the bank to work with a third party to identify and report suspicious transactions that went undetected. BofA had been working with regulators for some time to reach the resolutions, Borthwick said, adding the bank had added thousands of people to shore up its efforts to tackle money laundering. The Charlotte, North Carolina-based bank reported a profit of $6.9 billion, or 91 cents per share, for the three months ended September 30, compared with $8.3 billion, or $1.04 per share, a year earlier. Excluding the $1.2 billion regulatory settlement charge, BofA earned $1.08 per share, missing estimates of $1.10 per share, according to estimates compiled by LSEG. Wall Street analysts said the penalty would likely add to negative sentiment and raise concerns about expenses and the duration of the order. The penalty follows a 2024 consent order from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, which had required BofA to address shortcomings in its ability to police money laundering. Since late 2023, BofA has been working with US regulators to overhaul its safeguards against money laundering and other illegal transactions. NII SHINES AS DEALMAKING WEAKENS BofA's investment banking fees fell 11% to $1.8 billion in the quarter. The bank had last month projected a decline of at least 10%, as it wasn't well positioned in some businesses that saw more activity. Dealmaking also slowed in the reported quarter as a grinding bond market rout and equities volatility weighed on activity. "There's a period in volatility like that where buyers and sellers just need to readjust valuations and expectations. So that always happens," Borthwick said, referring to the move in interest rates. Investment banking fees can be lumpy from quarter-to-quarter and are influenced by when deals close. Transaction timing can often move around due to market conditions and regulatory approvals. "The environment for deal making remains solid. It's a pretty active environment," Borthwick said, adding that BofA's investment banking pipelines are strong. BofA slipped to fourth place in the global investment banking league table for the first nine months of 2026, from third in the same period a year earlier, Dealogic data showed. In a bright spot, net interest income (NII) — the difference between what a bank earns on loans and pays out on deposits — jumped 8% in the quarter, driven by higher loan and deposit balances and fixed-rate asset repricing. BofA expects interest income to improve sequentially in the fourth-quarter. Full-year NII growth is anticipated to be 8% or more in 2027.

item.title: Putin convenes top Russian officials to discuss cybersecurity
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin will discuss cybersecurity with top officials on Wednesday, the Kremlin said, describing it as an increasingly pressing issue but denying the meeting was prompted by a spate of Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian data centres.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin will discuss cybersecurity with top officials on Wednesday, the Kremlin said, describing it as an increasingly pressing issue but denying the meeting was prompted by a spate of Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian data centres. "Artificial intelligence technologies bring many benefits and advantages, boosting efficiency. But at the same time, of course, attempts by various states to weaponize these new technologies... pose threats to entire sectors of any country's economy," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters. "Naturally, we are no exception, and we must be prepared for these challenges. That is why the president is holding this meeting today." Peskov said the meeting was not connected with Ukrainian drone strikes in the past week on [USN:L8N46009S TEXT:"four Russian data centres"] - three belonging to tech group Yandex and one to Sberbank. "No, this is a much more systemic meeting. It is not connected to those specific, isolated attacks," he said. The participants will include government ministers, top security officials, the head of Sberbank, and central bank governor Elvira Nabiullina, Peskov added.

item.title: TSX falls from three-week peak as hot US inflation weighs
item.description: Canada's main stock index pulled back sharply from a three-week high on Wednesday, as weaker metal prices weighed on miners, while hot US inflation data for September increased odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike later this month and put further pressure.
item.dc:creator: Anand R
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index pulled back sharply from a three-week high on Wednesday, as weaker metal prices weighed on miners, while hot US inflation data for September increased odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike later this month and put further pressure. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) was down 0.94% at 35,648.22 points by 10:31 a.m. ET. US [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer prices"] accelerated in September on higher gasoline costs, boosting expectations for a rate hike later this month Traders are pricing in a 46% chance of a quarter-point rate hike from the Fed on October 28, according to LSEG compiled data Materials sector (.GSPTTMT) was the biggest drag on the index, declining 3.9% as precious metal prices fell further after the data The rate sensitive financial sector (.SPTTFS) , which constitutes heavyweight banks also fell 0.8% "Canada will join other global central banks in hiking interest rates, but don't think they're going to deliver as much as futures or the bond market is currently expecting," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones Energy sector (.SPTTEN) , up 0.4%, limited losses, as oil prices held firm over $100 per barrel Reuters reported that Iran was using new tactics to target ships, seeking to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections Yields in the Canadian benchmark 10-year bond rose to 3.91% Canada is [USN:L4N4600EH TEXT:"pursuing "]a trade pact with India and closer EU ties to reduce reliance on the US, ahead of Indian PM Narendra Modi's visit in [USN:S0N44S00M TEXT:"December"] Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings (FFH.TO) will buy a [USN:L1N4600FH TEXT:"majority"] stake in India's IDBI Bank (IDBI.NS) in a deal worth 528.78 billion Indian rupees ($5.56 billion), the Indian government said. Shares were down 1.3%

item.title: Colombia opens embassy in Jerusalem, restores free trade deal with Israel
item.description: Colombia opened its embassy in Jerusalem on Wednesday, becoming the 10th government to do so, as new President Abelardo De La Espriella reversed his predecessor's break with Israel.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colombia opened its embassy in Jerusalem on Wednesday, becoming the 10th government to do so, as new [USN:L6N42U03W TEXT:"President Abelardo De La Espriella"] reversed his predecessor's break with Israel. Most countries maintain embassies to Israel in Tel Aviv. Israel regards Jerusalem as its capital, while Palestinians seek East Jerusalem as the capital of a future independent state. The city's status remains one of the most contentious issues in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict Former Colombian President Gustavo Petro [USN:S0N3D0083 TEXT:"broke diplomatic relations"] with Israel in 2024 over its actions in Gaza and had heavily criticised Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Petro also halted coal exports to Israel Petro closed Colombia's embassy in Tel Aviv and recalled its ambassador, a move Israel said was antisemitic and a reward for Hamas militants Right-winger De La Espriella became president in August. On Tuesday, the free trade agreement terminated by Petro was reinstated Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said that "opening an embassy in Jerusalem is not only recognition of the simple political fact that Jerusalem is Israel's capital. It is also recognition of a historical truth that no honest person can deny" "Today, we are taking a concrete step towards restoring diplomatic relations between our countries, relations that should never have been broken. Israel is a strategic partner. It always has been, and from now on, it will be an even stronger one," Colombian Minister of Foreign Affairs Omar Bula said at the opening Israel's Foreign Ministry noted that Saar and Bula will hold bilateral talks on Wednesday. The Colombian foreign ministry said in a statement the meeting will focus on political dialogue, security and defence cooperation, the strengthening of trade and new opportunities for investment Various governments have relocated their embassies to Jerusalem since the US [USN:KBN1I810Z TEXT:"did so in 2018"], including Guatemala, Honduras, Paraguay and [USN:L8N41W1DS TEXT:"Somaliland"] Palestinian Vice President Hussein Al Sheikh condemned the opening of the embassy. "We view it as a step that disregards international law and resolutions of international legitimacy, violating the special legal and historical status of the Holy City", he said in a statement

item.title: BlackRock draws $205 billion in client funds as quarterly profit beats estimates
item.description: BlackRock surpassed Wall Street profit expectations and attracted $205 billion in total inflows in the third quarter, sending the world's largest asset manager's shares up as much as 5% in trading on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Utkarsh Shetti, Suzanne McGee
item.content:encoded: BlackRock (BLK.N) surpassed Wall Street profit expectations and attracted $205 billion in total inflows in the third quarter, sending the world's largest asset manager's shares up as much as 5% in trading on Wednesday. CEO Larry Fink credited the ongoing strength in the benchmark US stock market index, the Standard & Poor's 500, for the company's ability to trounce analysts' expectations for revenue and profit growth during the just-ended third quarter. As the index extended its gains, ending the period near its all-time highs, BlackRock posted a 38% gain in earnings per share and reported that revenues grew to $7.8 billion, well above consensus forecasts of $7.5 billion. "Market fundamentals are strong and well supported, with higher margins and earnings momentum catalyzed by new technology," CEO Larry Fink said in a statement. When markets opened for trading on Wednesday morning with major indexes in negative territory, BlackRock was trading 0.8% higher while shares of rival asset management companies tumbled. That marks a turnaround for BlackRock, whose shares have failed to keep pace with the broader market this year, amid fears that growing investor caution might curb earnings or revenue growth. Instead, BlackRock reported that its assets under management — which determine a large chunk of the earnings — rose to $15.49 trillion, from $13.46 trillion a year earlier and $15.34 trillion in the second quarter. The growth was driven by a combination of $134.5 billion of new flows into BlackRock's flagship iShares ETFs, and the rising valuations of its investments in a robust equity market. The company's adjusted profit of $15.93 per share beat Wall Street expectations of $14.13, according to data compiled by LSEG. Even as markets have remained resilient, surging bond yields and the expectation that the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike marks the beginning of a tightening cycle have dented investor confidence. During a call to discuss the results, however, BlackRock CFO Martin Small said that the market is evolving. "I don't believe we can evaluate the investment environment as risk-on or risk-off any longer," he said. Instead, he described it as one characterized by "capital scarcity, higher long-term yields, and a redesign of diversification." Despite higher yields and falling bond prices, BlackRock reported that net flows into its debt products totaled $78.2 billion in the third quarter. AI FINANCING PUSH BlackRock is among the most significant financiers of the AI boom, having inked partnerships with the likes of Microsoft and Meta, aiming to capitalize on the mammoth spending commitments undertaken by hyperscalers. On the post-earnings call with analysts, Fink compared the early stages of the AI buildout to the launch of the mortgage securities market in the 1980s, a market segment now worth trillions of dollars. Ultimately, he said, it will be possible to translate compute capacity into tradable securitized products. Fink described compute capacity as an "asset class" in its own right. The development of a data series tracking AI metrics will broaden investor demand for new securitized products tied to the fledgling asset class, he added, noting that BlackRock already possesses "data at scale" and plans to be a key player. Meanwhile, demand for capital to fund the costly AI rollout, coupled with ballooning government deficits, has increased the competition for capital, Fink said. PRIVATE CREDIT FOCUS BlackRock has accelerated its push into private credit markets in recent years. The asset class typically generates higher fees than its main source of profits, its suite of ETFs. The company previously spelled out plans to deliver more than $35 billion in revenue by the end of the decade, with over 30% of that coming from private markets and technology. Fink said that in the last 12 months, BlackRock has raised a total of $68 billion for investment in private markets broadly, with $25 billion for private credit, which he said investors view as "an increasingly attractive source of yield and portfolio diversification." He added that he expects investor demand to continue to rise heading into 2027. The private credit industry has recently come under scrutiny from investors concerned about lenders' exposure to AI-related disruption as well as opaque valuations, a wariness that prompted a surge in redemption requests from investors in recent quarters. That pressure, however, seems to be easing, with many private credit fund managers reporting redemption requests are slowing. While BlackRock does not break out its revenue from private markets, net flows in this category were $15.31 billion in the quarter.

item.title: Wall St slides as hot CPI data fuels rate-hike bets; chips, banks weigh
item.description: Wall Street's main indexes edged lower on Wednesday after a hotter-than-expected inflation report boosted bets of an interest rate hike this month, while investors parsed more big bank earnings.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: Wall Street's main indexes edged lower on Wednesday after a hotter-than-expected inflation report boosted bets of an interest rate hike this month, while investors parsed more big bank earnings. Data showed US consumer prices accelerated in September amid a surge in gasoline costs, leading traders to bolster bets of a rate hike in October. They now see a 46% chance of a quarter-point increase compared with a 21.6% chance before the figures, according to LSEG-compiled data. "It certainly increases the odds of the Federal Reserve raising rates at the October meeting, but I believe they're not going to, because we have never had two rate hikes within two months of midterm election," said Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA Research. Stovall said given the Fed had taken a hawkish stance on monetary policy, the data makes a December rate hike increasingly likely. Markets also digested another round of bank earnings. Bank of America (BAC.N) was down 8.5% after the lender's [USN:L4N4600WF TEXT:"profit fell"] in the third quarter as it set aside $1.2 billion to cover regulatory fines, while Morgan Stanley (MS.N) dipped 3.4% despite a [USN:L4N4600Y8 TEXT:"rise in quarterly profit"]. The S&P 500 Banks index (.SPXBK) fell 2.4% to its lowest level in over four months. Asset manager BlackRock (BLK.N) gained 2% after reporting a jump in[USN:L4N4600US TEXT:" third-quarter profit"], helped by higher fees from managing client funds. At 10:09 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 32.80 points, or 0.06%, to 51,637.30, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 46.65 points, or 0.60%, to 7,758.80 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 216.07 points, or 0.78%, to 26,988.31. Seven of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors declined. Sectors considered traditionally defensive rose, with consumer staples (.SPLRCS) and healthcare (.SPXHC) stocks up 0.9% and 1.7%, respectively. The S&P 500 technology index (.SPLRCT) was trading at over two-week lows, as chip stocks came under pressure again. They lost ground on Tuesday after reports pointing to progress in chip design by China's CXMT (688825.SS) fueled competition concerns. Shares of Intel (INTC.O) and Micron (MU.O) fell 2.6% and 1%, respectively, while Nvidia (NVDA.O) slipped 1.7%. Most "Magnificent Seven" stocks declined, barring Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Apple (AAPL.O) , which rose 0.2% and 0.9%, respectively. Remarks from Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin and the Fed's Beige Book report on regional economic conditions are also due late in the day. Oil prices[USN:L1N46003I TEXT:" edged higher"] on Wednesday, with Brent crude holding above the $100-a-barrel mark after two vessels were struck in the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying new tactics to target ships. Among individual movers, Liquidia (LQDA.O) jumped 28% after the drugmaker said it [USN:L6N4600JH TEXT:"settled all six pending lawsuits"] with United Therapeutics (UTHR.O) , ensuring uninterrupted access to Yutrepia, a drug used to treat patients with a form of pulmonary hypertension. Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 5.57-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 3.3-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 11 new 52-week highs and 9 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 16 new highs and 309 new lows.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities after Aramco HQ hit
item.description: The Houthis said the threatened locations were legitimate targets.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Jana Choukeir, Tala Ramadan
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Houthis vowed on Wednesday to press on with attacks on airports and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia, a day after a strike that sources said caused [USN:L6N4600QH TEXT:"extensive damage"] to the headquarters of oil giant [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"Saudi Aramco"] (2223.SE) . The Houthis said the threatened locations were legitimate targets and described their attacks as retaliation for Saudi strikes on Yemen - threatening to escalate a conflict reignited by the US-Iran confrontation in the Gulf. Saudi Arabia has faced widening [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"Houthi"] strikes over the past week, including [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"an attack"] on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday that killed 13 people. Tuesday night's attack on Saudi Aramco's base in the eastern city of Dhahran caused a fire that spread across several floors, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters. The Saudi energy ministry had [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"said"] the strike caused a limited fire. Operations at Aramco were continuing normally, with employees working from home, according to two of the sources. Aramco did not immediately reply to a Reuters request for comment. SAUDI-LED FORCES SAY THEY INTERCEPT MISSILE The escalating conflict has dealt a blow to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's ambitious plans to transform and diversify the Saudi economy and reduce its reliance on oil. The Houthis say they have been retaliating for the kingdom's backing of Yemeni government forces in the Yemen war that restarted last month. The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis towards Riyadh on Wednesday, and several loud booms were heard in the Saudi capital. Saudi authorities earlier issued an alert for a possible aerial threat in Riyadh on Wednesday before the warning was lifted, a witness said. It wasn't immediately clear what caused the booms and there was no immediate comment from the authorities on their source. The Saudi government media office didn't immediately respond to a request for comment about the cause of the booms. In their statement on Wednesday, the Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones at the Saudi Aramco facilities in Dhahran, Riyadh airport and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh. In a broad threat, they urged "international shipping companies", civilians and workers to evacuate Saudi airports and oil facilities. The Dhahran complex hosts a major operations centre for Aramco, which oversees a vast network of onshore and offshore oil rigs, pipelines, refineries and export terminals. Riyadh’s international airport has come under attack four times, including Saturday's attack which was the deadliest in Saudi Arabia in a decade. Authorities have [USN:L6N45Y0C1 TEXT:"closed the airport "]until October 17, and [USN:L6N45Z0WM TEXT:"airlines"] have canceled flights to Saudi Arabia. Fearing the rise of Iranian influence and the prospect of chaos on its borders, Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen's civil war in support of the government in 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa. The UN brokered a 2022 truce between the warring sides in Yemen that kept a fragile peace until this year. Saudi Arabia resumed its military campaign in Yemen in support of the internationally recognised government in a bid to reverse the Houthis' sudden gains last month, when they swept down the Red Sea coast to the critical Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The [USN:L6N4600LK TEXT:"Red Cross "]said on Wednesday that hospitals across Yemen are struggling to cope with a sharp rise in war casualties as fighting intensified along multiple front lines. The UN World Food Programme warned that life-saving assistance had been cut off to the government-held city of [USN:L1N45Z0S1 TEXT:"Taiz"], which was encircled by Houthi fighters earlier this month. "WFP and its partners cannot access more than 600,000 people in Taiz who depend on humanitarian assistance, including more than 200,000 women and children," WFP said in a statement.

item.title: China's Hesai launches spatial camera to boost AI-powered robotics adoption
item.description: Hesai Group , a leading Chinese autonomous driving technology firm, on Wednesday unveiled a three-dimensional mapping camera, targeting demand for physical spatial data needed to train the AI systems powering humanoid robots.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hesai Group (2525.HK) , a leading Chinese autonomous driving technology firm, on Wednesday unveiled a three-dimensional mapping camera, targeting demand for physical spatial data needed to train the AI systems powering humanoid robots. The company introduced "Kosmo," a device resembling a wine bottle, that combines lidar sensors and cameras to help developers collect real-world spatial data more efficiently. There is a significant gap in high-quality spatial data needed to train AI-powered robots to understand and interact with the real world and perform complex tasks beyond waving arms or dancing, Hesai co-founder and CEO David Li said at a launch event at the company's Shanghai factory. Li said robots remain limited in their ability to solve real productivity challenges. Most robots are still confined to low-impact functions like greeting guests, waving or dancing, he said. "What we aim to offer is essentially a platform for the underlying technologies required by the robotics industry, positioning Hesai as a tier 1 supplier comparable to Bosch in the automotive sector, or perhaps even beyond," Li said. He declined to provide revenue projections for Kosmo but said the firm has signed agreements with Chinese robotics firms to use the product. Hesai has also been developing robot actuators, which convert electricity into mechanical motion and account for more than half of a robot's material costs, Li said. Demand is growing for actuators that are lighter, smaller and more precise, allowing robots to become more safe and agile, he added. The actuators are already being used by Sharpa Robotics, a startup founded by Hesai's co-founders, in its flagship robotic hand, Sharpa Wave. A Sharpa Wave robot has been autonomously serving ice cream at a Dairy Queen outlet in Shanghai. Hesai said Kosmo's detailed mapping technology helped the robot achieve a task success rate of 99%. Sharpa Robotics, which recently raised more than 4.5 billion yuan ($672.4 million) in a funding round, operates independently of Hesai, but provides a testing ground for the company's robotics technologies. In automotive markets, Hesai has become the world's largest lidar supplier for autonomous vehicles over the past three years, driving the cost of the technology [USN:L3N3MX0MP TEXT:"below $200"] per unit. Its customers include Mercedes-Benz (MBGn.DE) , Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) , General Motors (GM.N) and Ford Motor (F.N) . ($1 = 6.6923 Chinese yuan renminbi)

item.title: Edison CEO says EDF has paused stake sale plan as Qatar LNG uncertainty persists
item.description: France's EDF has put plans to sell a stake in its Italian subsidiary Edison on hold due to uncertainty over gas supplies from Qatar, Edison's chief executive said on Wednesday, adding that the process could resume early next year.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Landini
item.content:encoded: France's EDF has put plans to sell a stake in its Italian subsidiary Edison (EDNn.MI) on hold due to uncertainty over gas supplies from Qatar, Edison's chief executive said on Wednesday, adding that the process could resume early next year. The prolonged conflict between the United States and Iran has disrupted energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, where around one-fifth of global liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies passed before the war. In its last official notice, QatarEnergy said it would not deliver cargoes to Edison until at least the first [USN:S8N40Y05J TEXT:"half of December"]. Edison has been forced to replace Qatari supply, which accounted for around 40% of the group's portfolio, since April, with CEO Nicola Monti saying it had mostly been buying US LNG on the spot market. "At the moment, neither we nor, it seems, QatarEnergy are in a position to make longer-term forecasts. We hope deliveries can resume at the beginning of next year, but we have no visibility at this stage," Monti said at an energy conference organised by Italian publisher RCS. EDF has for months [USN:L2N3VP0RS TEXT:"been studying"] an IPO or the sale of a minority stake in Edison to investors as it seeks to raise funds to finance the construction of new reactors and maintain its ageing domestic fleet. As obstacles to the transaction emerged, EDF turned to the United States, where it sold its [USN:L6N4321BP TEXT:"renewable power assets"] for $4.2 billion. "We are ready to resume the (stake sale) process... I expect we will restart it next year, once there is greater clarity in the markets, particularly over the situation in the Gulf," Monti said. The Edison CEO said that the company was not interested in terminating its 25-year contract with QatarEnergy, which it signed in 2009 for the annual supply of 6.4 billion cubic meters of natural gas. "Relations with QatarEnergy are excellent... we are therefore keen to understand when discussions can resume and how the contract might be extended for several more years."

item.title: Yemen fighting overwhelms hospitals, cuts aid to 800,000 people, relief agencies say
item.description: Hospitals across Yemen are struggling to cope with a sharp rise in war casualties, while intensified fighting along multiple front lines has cut off vital aid to around 800,000 people, humanitarian agencies said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Hospitals across Yemen are struggling to cope with a sharp rise in war casualties, while intensified fighting along multiple front lines has cut off vital aid to around 800,000 people, humanitarian agencies said on Wednesday. Aid agencies are warning of rapidly worsening conditions in Yemen since war resumed between the Iran-allied [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"Houthis"] and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government last month, a conflict reignited by the US-Iran confrontation in the Gulf. In [USN:L1N45Z0S1 TEXT:"Taiz"], a government-held city that was encircled by Houthi fighters earlier this month, wheat flour stocks are nearly exhausted, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) said on Wednesday. Remaining food supplies may not last long if access constraints continue, it said, adding that more than 600,000 people in Taiz depend on aid, including more than 200,000 children. Medical supplies are also running low. One hospital in Taiz said it faces severe shortages of dialysis supplies and its stocks would last 14 days. "A shipment from Aden was scheduled, but due to the current situation, we were unable to receive it," Yussef al-Zakari, head of the kidney center at al-Thawra Hospital, told Reuters. Kidney patient Maamun Abdulwahad Naaman, who receives dialysis treatment twice a week at the hospital, said he could not return to his village some 15 km (10 miles) from Taiz city due to clashes on the road. "If I stay at home, I cannot return to the kidney hospital (centre), and my condition will deteriorate if I remain there," he said. The WFP said a total of 800,000 people were beyond its reach in Yemen. "This is the kind of situation that can rapidly spiral into a humanitarian catastrophe if assistance cannot move safely and reach those who need it most," El-Khidir Daloum, WFP Representative and Country Director in Yemen, said in a statement. The Red Cross said front-line hospitals in areas including Marib, [USN:L1N45Z0S1 TEXT:"Taiz"] and Yemen's Red Sea coast are seeing unprecedented numbers of weapon-wounded patients, with some facilities admitting more than 700 casualties in a single week. More than [USN:L6N45T0PA TEXT:"200,000 people have been displaced"] from their homes since fighting in the country began in recent weeks, according to the United Nations' International Organization for Migration. "Trauma care staff are under enormous pressure," ICRC health coordinator Feras Abusamra said in a statement. Only a small proportion of Yemen's functioning health facilities are capable of providing comprehensive trauma care, he said, while hospitals face large numbers of wounded people amid shortages of surgical supplies, anesthesia, oxygen and medicines. Yemen's health services, battered by more than a decade of conflict, economic crisis, displacement and disease outbreaks, may have limited capacity to absorb a new surge in mass casualties if fighting intensifies further, the ICRC warned.

item.title: GSK plans to cut up to 1,217 jobs in Belgium as it begins three-year restructuring plan
item.description: GSK said on Wednesday it could cut as many as 1,217 jobs in Belgium, in the first sign that the British drugmaker's three-year plan to save £1.9 billion ($2.50 billion) in costs is moving into action.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: GSK (GSK.L) said on Wednesday it could cut as many as 1,217 jobs in Belgium, in the first sign that the British drugmaker's three-year plan to save £1.9 billion ($2.50 billion) in costs is moving into action. CEO Luke Miels had launched [USN:L6N43U0QG TEXT:"the effort in July"] as part of a broader push to speed up drug development and reassure investors that GSK can manage an approaching patent cliff for its blockbuster HIV drug dolutegravir. Changes include simplifying the company's research, manufacturing and support operations, including through increased use of digital tools and more automation. The proposed cuts would affect some of its more than 8,000 employees at sites in Rixensart, Wavre and Gembloux, but would not include factory workers. Globally, GSK had 66,841 employees at the end of last year, according to its annual report. GSK said it will remain the country's largest biopharmaceutical sector employer and that Belgium will continue to produce the majority of its vaccines. Shares in the company were up 2.6% at 1430 GMT, in line with broader sector gains. The plans were presented to unions earlier on Wednesday, Belgian newspaper L'Echo reported. Unions did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment. The company expects the proposed changes will help its factories to better match demand for some of its established vaccines. [USN:L4N4531CJ TEXT:"Last month"], GSK said it plans to shut down a vaccine factory in Dresden, Germany next year citing decreased demand for egg-based flu vaccines. GSK will continue working with Belgian universities and research centres but focus R&D resources on high-priority projects, including its mRNA flu vaccine, it said on Wednesday. ($1 = 0.7594 pounds)

item.title: Des frappes russes font six morts en Ukraine, les infrastructures énergétiques visées
item.description: Des bombardements russes ont fait six morts et des dizaines de blessés mercredi à Kyiv, la capitale ukrainienne, et à Loutsk, dans l'ouest du pays, ont déclaré les autorités qui font état de dommages sur nombre d'infrastructures énergétiques.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des bombardements russes ont fait six morts et des dizaines de blessés mercredi à Kyiv, la capitale ukrainienne, et à Loutsk, dans l'ouest du pays, ont déclaré les autorités qui font état de dommages sur nombre d'infrastructures énergétiques. Une première attaque au cours de la nuit, menée avec des missiles balistiques et des drones, a duré plusieurs heures et a visé Kyiv, où trois personnes sont mortes, et Kharkiv, la deuxième plus grande ville d'Ukraine, a précisé le président Volodimir Zelensky, suggérant que Moscou se moquait des efforts de paix du président américain Donald Trump. Les attaques ont endommagé 30 installations énergétiques du pays et au moins 600.000 personnes se sont retrouvées sans électricité dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi, a-t-il ajouté. Une autre attaque mercredi matin a visé la ville de Loutsk, à une centaine de kilomètres de la frontière polonaise, tuant trois personnes et en blessant au moins 12. Selon le gouverneur de la région, Roman Romaniouk, des débris de drone ont touché un entrepôt et un immeuble résidentiel a également été endommagé. Volodimir Zelensky a également estimé injuste le fait que Kyiv ait une nouvelle fois été frappée sans que l'Ukraine n'ait été prévenue au préalable par ses partenaires occidentaux. Le président américain Donald Trump, qui a annoncé dimanche la conclusion d'un accord de [USN:L8N45X03P TEXT:"cessez-le-feu énergétique"] entre l'Ukraine et la Russie, a assuré mardi que Washington continuait de partager des renseignements avec Kyiv et que les efforts de son administration pour mettre fin à la guerre se poursuivaient. "Les faits montrent que les Russes ne se considèrent pas tenus de respecter ce qu'a déclaré le président des États-Unis", a encore dit Volodimir Zelensky par allusion à la présumée trêve énergétique entre les deux pays. "Cette frappe était tout à fait délibérée et son ampleur était une véritable démonstration de force : la Russie n'avait jamais auparavant fait preuve d’un tel mépris manifeste envers les États-Unis", a encore dit le président ukrainien. Le ministère russe de la Défense a dit pour sa part que ses forces avaient frappé sept infrastructures énergétiques ukrainiennes, dont plusieurs à Kyiv, lors d'une attaque massive menée pendant la nuit. Moscou a également frappé un centre de données situé dans la capitale ukrainienne qui, selon le ministère, servait à recueillir des renseignements sur les forces armées russes. L'Ukraine a quant à elle visé, à l'aide de drones, le plus grand centre de données de Russie. Cette frappe contre le centre de données de Balakovo, propriété de Sberbank dans le sud de la Russie, fait suite à trois attaques menées la semaine dernière contre des centres de données appartenant au groupe technologique russe Yandex. RESTRICTIONS DE STARLINK EN UKRAINE Selon Serhii Beskrestnov, conseiller auprès du ministère ukrainien de la Défense, SpaceX a imposé une restriction sur certains services de son réseau Starlink en Ukraine, suspendant le fonctionnement de sa version de niveau militaire à des vitesses supérieures à 160 km/h, ce qui perturbe les missions de combat. "Nos forces de défense n'ont reçu aucun avertissement concernant cette restriction, ce qui a entraîné la perturbation de plusieurs missions", a-t-il dit sur Telegram. Les terminaux internet par satellite de SpaceX, société dirigée par le milliardaire Elon Musk, proche de Donald Trump, sont indispensables pour guider les frappes de drones à longue portée menées par l'Ukraine, qui ont freiné l'effort de guerre russe. Starlink n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaire. Le moins bon fonctionnement de ses services intervient à un moment où Washington fait pression sur l'Ukraine pour cesser ses frappes sur les raffineries russes. Pour tenter d'enrayer la machine de guerre russe, aux équipements plus modernes et aux troupes plus nombreuses, l'Ukraine a adopté la stratégie de frapper des [USN:L6N45P05R TEXT:"raffineries"], poussant Moscou à suspendre ses exportations de diesel et provoquant depuis plusieurs semaines la colère de Donald Trump. Sans mentionner l'impact de la guerre qu'il mène contre l'Iran, Donald Trump a accusé à plusieurs reprises l'Ukraine d'être responsable de la flambée des prix du diesel aux Etats-Unis, un motif de mécontentement majeur pour de nombreux Américains et donc un sujet d'inquiétude au sein de son camp républicain à l'approche des élections législatives de mi-mandat le 3 novembre. L'armée de l'air ukrainienne a précisé que les défenses aériennes du pays avaient abattu quatre des 39 missiles balistiques lancés par la Russie au cours de la nuit, un ratio qui illustre le manque criant de systèmes d'interception dont souffre l'Ukraine. Volodimir Zelensky était mercredi en Grande-Bretagne, où le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham et le roi Charles devaient manifester leur soutien au président ukrainien après la détérioration brutale de ses relations avec les États-Unis. Andy Burnham s'engagera à fournir un nouveau lot de missiles sol-air alors que la Grande-Bretagne a déclaré ne pas soutenir l'accord entre les États-Unis et la Russie sur le diesel et appelé ses alliés à maintenir la pression économique sur Moscou. "Mon message au peuple ukrainien ne saurait être plus clair : nous sommes à vos côtés aussi longtemps qu'il le faudra, et nous irons plus loin et plus vite dans notre soutien pour appuyer votre combat courageux en faveur de la paix en Europe", a déclaré le Premier ministre britannique dans un communiqué avant sa rencontre avec Volodimir Zelensky.

item.title: Stripchat loses legal fight against EU tech label
item.description: Adult content platform Stripchat, a subsidiary of Cyprus's Technius, on Thursday lost its legal challenge against EU tech regulators' decision to include it in a list of companies subject to stringent requirements under landmark online content rules after Europe's second-highest court rejected its arguments, a court statement said.
item.dc:creator: Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: Adult content platform Stripchat, a subsidiary of Cyprus's Technius, on Thursday lost its legal challenge against EU tech regulators' decision to include it in a list of companies subject to stringent requirements under landmark online content rules after Europe's second-highest court rejected its arguments, a court statement said. Three years ago, the European Commission designated Stripchat and two other adult content companies as very large online platforms under the Digital Services Act which requires such companies to do more to tackle illegal and harmful content on their platforms. DSA breaches can cost companies fines as much as 6% of their global turnover. Stripchat subsequently sued the Commission, which is the EU tech enforcer, at the Luxembourg-based General Court. It disagreed with how the Commission calculated its number of users, a benchmark used to assess whether a company falls under the DSA. A court statement stated that the European Commission had given Stripchat adequate reasons for its decision. The ruling can be appealed on matters of law at the EU Court of Justice, Europe's top court. The case is T-134/24 Technius v Commission.

item.title: Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis
item.description: Pope Leo's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday, after doctors announced the 71-year-old pontiff was being treated for lung cancer.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: Pope Leo's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday, after doctors announced the 71-year-old pontiff was being treated for [USN:L8N46006S TEXT:"lung cancer"]. World leaders, Catholics across the globe and senior cardinals at the Vatican have offered prayers for Leo after he had part of his right lung removed in an operation on Tuesday. Blood tests and a chest X-ray carried out on Wednesday showed normal post-operative results, the Vatican said, adding that the pontiff had undergone respiratory physiotherapy. The cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be relatively young and energetic and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and [USN:L8N4600P9 TEXT:"raised questions"] about the future shape of his papacy as he deals with the illness. Leo normally follows a very busy schedule. He is due to make a tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17 and the Vatican press office said on Wednesday that "nothing has changed" regarding the planned trip. The pope is the ultimate earthly authority for the world's 1.4 billion Catholics and does not have a deputy who steps in when he is sick. When a pope is incapacitated, the business of the Vatican's vast bureaucracy carries on as usual, holding off on any decisions that require papal approval. PRAYERS FOR LEO A prayer was recited for Leo to have a good convalescence and complete healing during an open-air Mass in St. Peter's Square on Wednesday following the surgery. The pope has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung during Tuesday's operation in an effort to eliminate all cancerous tissue. Human lungs have five lobes — three in the right lung and two in the left. The operation lasted about 90 minutes and was completed without complications, the pope's lead surgeon, Stefano Margaritora, and his personal physician, Luigi Carbone, said late on Tuesday. The Vatican has not disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis. Leo is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to have had recent health issues. BEST WISHES AND PRAYERS The Vatican said this week that the pope was expected to remain in hospital for about a week and that all his public engagements had been cancelled until October 20. The Mass on Wednesday was the closing act of an assembly of bishops called by Leo to discuss the Church's family life teachings, the largest gathering of Church leaders so far during this papacy. Filipino [USN:L8N45V0O6 TEXT:"Cardinal Luis Tagle"] led the service in place of Leo. The pope last week approved Tagle as the dean of the Church's College of Cardinals, in the first selection of an Asian cleric to the elite role. Political leaders offered messages of support. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he and his wife Jeanette were praying for the pope, an American who was born in Chicago. "May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father," he said on X. Rubio [USN:L1N41K0C6 TEXT:"met Leo"] at the Vatican in May. There was no immediate response on social media from US President Donald Trump, who has criticised the pope, or from Vice President JD Vance, who is a Catholic.

item.title: South African rand slides as US inflation print boosts Fed tightening bets
item.description: The South African rand weakened sharply on Wednesday after a hotter-than-expected US inflation reading boosted expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates later this month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The South African rand weakened sharply on Wednesday after a hotter-than-expected US inflation reading boosted expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates later this month. At 1415 GMT, the rand traded at 16.62 against the dollar , about 0.8% weaker than its previous close. The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose to 102.87, up 0.7% on Tuesday's close. The US Consumer Price Index [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"rose 0.6%"] last month after climbing 0.4% in August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Wednesday. Markets see about a 44% chance of a US rate hike this month, up from about 22% before the inflation data, and are pricing a 95% probability of an increase in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool . With no major domestic data due, the rand takes its cue from global developments, particularly US economic indicators and geopolitical events. On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the Top-40 index (.JTOPI) was last down 1%. South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond strengthened, as the yield fell 2 basis points to 8.74%.

item.title: IMF urges members to stock up funds for low-income, vulnerable states
item.description: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva on Wednesday warned that current economic developments and the rapid advance of AI threaten to deepen the gulf between advanced and developing economies, especially given steep drops in development assistance.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, David Lawder
item.content:encoded: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva on Wednesday warned that current economic developments and the rapid advance of AI threaten to deepen the gulf between advanced and developing economies, especially given steep drops in development assistance. Georgieva, the first IMF chief from a developing country, said higher benchmark yields in advanced economies were spilling over to emerging markets and low-income countries. Average debt service costs had increased to 14% of revenue from 6% a decade ago, even as overall debt burdens have eased, she said. "The risk of divergence is most dangerous for those that are already further behind," she told a press conference during the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand, amid a growing chorus of concern about the worsening impact of global economic developments on [USN:L4N4600BS TEXT:"developing countries"]. She said the International Monetary Fund recognized its responsibility to help finance countries when needed, and urged IMF member states to make good their pledges to increase funding for its Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust, which provides low- and zero-interest loans to low-income countries. The IMF was also asking members to replenish the Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust, a fund that provides grants for debt-service relief and cancellation to the poorest and most vulnerable member countries, she said. Higher fuel and food costs, declining development assistance and subdued appetite for riskier investments were piling pressure on many of these countries, despite years of "hard work," Georgieva said. The IMF this week flagged significant growth and financial stability risks from a potential end of the AI investment boom, growing debt levels and a prolonged Middle East conflict. It [USN:L1N45X05U TEXT:"forecast global growth at 3.1% for 2026"]. Nearly all developing economies were expected to see slower growth in 2026, it said. DEBT COSTS A BARRIER TO GROWTH Officials from developing countries are warning that rising debt service costs, estimated at [USN:L1N45Z04L TEXT:"$500 billion"] more than for advanced economies, pose a major barrier to inclusive growth. "This puts a lot of burden on us because not only are we not able to invest in our infrastructure space or build the human capital formation, but debt service becomes a mandatory requirement," Gambian Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs Seedy Keita said. He noted the IMF was currently collecting more from loans to its members than it was lending, while developing countries were struggling with weaker balance sheets. Cameroon's finance minister, Louis Paul Motaze, speaking on behalf of more than a dozen other sub-Saharan African countries, said developing economies would continue to need support from international financial institutions, echoing Georgieva's call for member states to top up funding for the PRGT and CCRT funds. "Domestic resource mobilization, stronger debt management, and deeper domestic capital markets are indispensable, but domestic efforts alone may not be sufficient to close widening financing gaps," he said in a statement to the International Monetary and Financial Committee released on Wednesday. "Predictable concessional financing, stronger mobilization of private capital, and effective catalytic support from international financial institutions remain critical," he said. Georgieva said the IMF had restructured the PRGT, its fund for low-income countries, to triple lending to the countries, but members needed to honour their funding commitments, giving no details on missed or delayed pledges. The IMF was also encouraging contributions to the CCRT, which she said was in urgent need of replenishment given frequent use of the facility in recent years.
