Georgieva said she was optimistic that Senegal, the latest country to seek relief under the Group of 20 Common Framework for Debt Treatments, would get through the restructuring process quickly, noting that the IMF had reached staff-level agreement on a $2.2 billion lending program for the West African country.

item.title: Kamala Harris warns window closing for AI safeguards, urges US-China cooperation
item.description: Former US Vice President Kamala Harris urged governments and technology companies on Wednesday to urgently put safeguards in place for artificial intelligence, warning that the window for containing its gravest risks was closing.
item.dc:creator: Kyu-Seok Shim
item.content:encoded: Former US Vice President Kamala Harris urged governments and technology companies on Wednesday to urgently put safeguards in place for artificial intelligence, warning that the window for containing its gravest risks was closing. "If we are to have any guardrails and safeguards, they have to be at the table," Harris said of AI developers during an appearance at South Korea's Asan Institute for Policy Studies. "My concern is that the window is shutting." Harris said governments and companies must act immediately against what she described as three existential dangers from AI - cybersecurity threats, AI-enabled weapons and systems escaping human control. She also urged the United States to engage China on international rules and standards for AI, saying their broader strategic rivalry should not preclude cooperation on shared risks. "There is room for cooperation where our interests are aligned," Harris said, calling for "healthy and robust competition, but not conflict." Harris criticised what she called US President Donald Trump's "erratic tariffs" and their punitive nature, before warning against a transactional approach that cost the US global influence. "The question is, are we thinking only about the short term, or do we also value and appreciate the significance of an investment for long-term gain?" Harris praised South Korean investment in US shipbuilding, semiconductors, electric vehicles and clean energy, calling it "immensely significant and valued". She also called for renewed US commitment to South Korea, saying growing cooperation among North Korea, Russia, China and Iran was very concerning and meant the allies must strengthen deterrence. The former vice president has been [USN:L6N45U0XV TEXT:"campaigning"] for Democratic candidates ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections as she weighs another White House bid. She said Democrats would win a majority in the House of Representatives and had a "very good shot" at taking the Senate, potentially giving Congress a stronger voice on domestic and foreign policy, including the war with Iran. Asked whether she would again seek the presidency in 2028, Harris said: "I'm still thinking about it. I haven’t decided yet."

item.title: Trump says massive oil, gas exploration set to begin in 'our Greenland'
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that "massive oil, gas and mineral exploration" was set to begin on Greenland, a contentious statement on a territory that has resisted his efforts to control it and has banned new drilling for crude.
item.dc:creator: Louise Rasmussen
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that "massive oil, gas and mineral exploration" was set to begin on Greenland, a contentious statement on a territory that has resisted his efforts to control it and has banned new drilling for crude. Trump described the Danish Arctic island which is run by a semi-autonomous government as "our new and beautiful Greenland" in a social media post that hailed what he said were US gains from [USN:L6N45E07X TEXT:"a security deal"] signed in September. The Greenlandic prime minister's office declined to comment on Trump's statement. The Danish foreign ministry and Greenland's ministry of mineral resources did not immediately respond to requests for comment. TRUMP HAILS US SECURITY GAINS Greenland has been caught up in [USN:L1N45D06G TEXT:"a confrontation"] with Trump who has been saying since 2019 the US should buy or take the strategically located and [USN:L1N3YF0UH TEXT:"mineral-rich island"] for security reasons. On several occasions, he refused to rule out force. Along with Denmark, the US and Greenland reached an agreement last month to allow the US to boost its military presence on the island - a deal that had appeared to settle the standoff. The agreement did not allocate any rights for mining or drilling. "Massive Oil, Gas, and Mineral Exploration is getting ready to begin," Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform. "There are Experts that are saying that the amount of easily available Oil is far greater than that of almost any land, anywhere in the World," he added without naming any specific deals or specific development. Greenland banned uranium mining in its territory along with all future exploration of oil in 2021. The government has said it is reviewing whether a Texas firm, Greenland Energy, can use permits predating that prohibition. The company said in August this year it [USN:L6N45F0P1 TEXT:"had plans to drill"] for oil in 2027 at an untested basin on Greenland's east coast, although it lacked its own permit to do so. The previous owner, ARCO, spent heavily on seismic work in the 1970s but never drilled. Independent Danish security policy advisor Jacob Kaarsbo said Trump's comments could be seen as a sign that his desire to control Greenland remained unchanged. "It is extremely dangerous to view this agreement between the Trump administration and Denmark as something that has altered Trump’s intentions," he said. The 10-page deal between the US, Denmark and Greenland paved the way for two new military bases and Trump's "Golden Dome" missile defence system, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination. "Any future attack on the United States will have to come across Greenland, where our Defense will routinely knock down drones, missiles, or any other form of weapon not yet even conceived," Trump said in his post on Wednesday. "It gives us time, location, and sightline, like nowhere else in the World!" he added.

item.title: IMF calls for US to cut deficits amid bond woes, urges China to shift away from exports
item.description: The United States cannot grow its way out of mounting public debt without tax or spending adjustments, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: The United States cannot grow its way out of mounting public debt without tax or spending adjustments, while China must pivot from export-led growth towards more domestic consumption, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday. Georgieva admonished the world's two largest economies to make painful policy changes to reduce growing fiscal and trade imbalances, as her fiscal affairs chief said inflation, high debt levels and rising yields had heightened the urgency for budget consolidation around the globe. Speaking at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Georgieva singled out advanced economies, namely the US and European countries, as the "worst offenders" on excessive debts, with higher benchmark yields spilling over to low-income countries that have already been forced by financial markets to rein in borrowing. Asked at a press conference whether the US needs tighter fiscal policy, Georgieva said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recognizes that US deficit and debt levels are too high and need to be made more sustainable. "The authorities very much rely on strong growth in the United States" to help reduce debt, Georgieva said. "At the Fund, we believe that growth of course helps, but it cannot deliver fast enough the necessary adjustments. So, some (fiscal) measures would be necessary." The call for more action to reduce debt was echoed in the IMF's [USN:L1N460042 TEXT:"Fiscal Monitor"] report on Wednesday, which warned that delays in an era of higher borrowing costs would only make the job harder in coming years. While that message is a perennial one from the IMF, Rodrigo Valdes, the head of the IMF's Fiscal Affairs department, said the surge in bond yields had left governments with little fiscal room to manoeuvre. "We dialled up the urgency of our message," he added. BESSENT NO-SHOW Bessent is not attending the annual meetings in Bangkok, despite this year's US presidency of the Group of 20 major economies, instead favouring domestic engagements as the US [USN:L1N45N0R3 TEXT:"midterm election"] campaign heats up. He has acted as a chief spokesman for President Donald Trump's economic policies, particularly touting the deep tax cuts passed last year by Republicans now trying to maintain control of the US Congress. G20 finance ministers are due to meet on the sidelines of the Bangkok meetings on Thursday. The US has used its G20 presidency to try to rally allies to take stronger action to counter China's [USN:L1N44T0JC TEXT:""non-market" economic policies"] that have led to [USN:L1N45T0MB TEXT:"excess industrial capacity"] and a flood of global exports. Asked about imbalances emanating from China, on a day when data showed it was on track to post a [USN:L6N46005Q TEXT:"record trade surplus"], Georgieva repeated longstanding advice to Beijing: "For surplus countries, what they need to do is increase domestic consumption. That clearly applies to China's growth model. Shift from exports more toward domestic consumption." Deficit countries need to save more and spend less, while Europe needs to invest more in competitiveness, she said. "To put it very simply, China needs to spend more, the US has to save more, and Europe has to invest more," Georgieva added. FRENCH FISCAL WORRIES This week's meetings have been dominated by worries about growing debt and rising bond yields and risks from the artificial intelligence boom. France, one of the advanced economies [USN:L8N45S1P0 TEXT:"worst hit"] by a global bond sell-off, needs to solve its own debt woes through fiscal consolidation, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said, effectively playing down speculation about an ECB intervention in the bond market. Asked at a CNN event in Bangkok whether the ECB was about to help France, Lagarde said it was [USN:L1N46002V TEXT:"up to Paris"] to soothe investors' nerves. "And for that one, the primary and first solution lies at home in France. And it has to do with fiscal policies," she said. The IMF has lauded Britain for taking steps toward consolidation, but made clear on Wednesday that it does not want London to accelerate the pace of fiscal consolidation. "Our recommendation is 'stay the course'," Valdes said. Still, OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann called for "strong fiscal discipline" in a statement to the IMF's steering committee, saying this was needed to ensure stability. "In every G20 country except Germany and Türkiye, public debt as a share of GDP was higher in the first quarter of 2026 than at the end of 2007," he wrote to the International Monetary and Financial Committee. "Countries need to contain and reallocate spending, improve public-sector efficiency and make tax systems more effective. They should also protect investment that drives future growth, especially in education, skills and digital infrastructure." CALLS TO AID POOR COUNTRIES Regarding the growing divergence between advanced countries benefiting from AI investment and those bypassed by it, highlighted in Tuesday's IMF [USN:L1N45Z05I TEXT:"economic forecasts"], Georgieva also urged IMF member countries to [USN:L1N46004N TEXT:"fully fund"] IMF facilities for low-income and vulnerable countries. These include the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust, which provides low- and zero-interest loans to low-income countries, and the Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust, a fund that provides grants for debt-service relief and cancellation to the poorest and most vulnerable member countries, she said. These countries, too, were being squeezed by higher bond yields, with average debt service costs that have increased to 14% of revenue from 6% a decade ago, even as overall debt burdens have eased, she said. "The risk of divergence is most dangerous for those that are already further behind," Georgieva added.

item.title: Financial Stability Board should concentrate on genuinely systemic risks, review finds
item.description: The Financial Stability Board, the global watchdog for financial risks, should be more selective in prioritising new work and focus on vulnerabilities that are genuinely cross-border, cross-sectoral and systemic, a review of its processes found.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Financial Stability Board, the global watchdog for financial risks, should be more selective in prioritising new work and focus on vulnerabilities that are genuinely cross-border, cross-sectoral and systemic, a review of its processes found. The review, the findings of which were published on Wednesday, was commissioned to examine whether the FSB's approach to developing, drafting and presenting policy has itself created obstacles to implementation. It was conducted by the Independent Monitoring Review (IMR) group chaired by Randal Quarles, a former FSB chair and former US Federal Reserve vice chair for supervision and follows a 2025 report that noted a " concerning trend " of delayed or stalled implementation of FSB recommendations. The IMR found that national factors, including legal frameworks, market structures and political capacity, were the main reasons why implementation has lagged. It said the FSB's own processes had not always sufficiently accounted for those circumstances, in some cases making implementation more difficult or more contentious than necessary. The FSB should default to high-level principles when a vulnerability is still emerging, adding more detailed requirements only as its understanding of the risks develops, the IMR added. The FSB's recent work has included recommendations to improve cross-border payments and for the supervision of global stablecoins. It is also developing non-binding guidance for practices on AI use. Also on Wednesday, the FSB proposed eight recommendations that aim to modernise supervision frameworks.

item.title: IMF dials up calls for urgent fiscal consolidation
item.description: The International Monetary Fund on Wednesday issued an urgent call for advanced economies and others to reduce government spending, cut deficits and lower debt levels, warning that delays would only make the job harder in coming years.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: The International Monetary Fund on Wednesday issued an urgent call for advanced economies and others to reduce government spending, cut deficits and lower debt levels, warning that delays would only make the job harder in coming years. Rodrigo Valdes, head of the IMF's Fiscal Affairs department, said rising sovereign bond yields were adding to fiscal pressures at a time when average public debt was poised to hit 100% of gross domestic product, the highest seen since World War Two, leaving countries with less margin for delay. "We're saying now it's urgent and it's now because basically the conditions have changed," Valdes said, noting the risks posed by inflationary pressures, high levels of global debt and rising sovereign bond yields. "So, if you want one message, we dialed up the urgency of our message." Ahead of this week's annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, Valdes had told Reuters that "the fiscal results this year are worse than expected six months ago, and worse than they were one year ago." The majority of countries were now looking at boosting spending instead of tightening their belts, he said. NEED TO BUILD POLITICAL SUPPORT Valdes said the challenge for major advanced economies with high debt levels was to build political support for concrete plans to contain borrowing costs in the medium term, and limit spillovers to the rest of the world. "The more countries wait, the more painful the adjustment becomes," the IMF said in a blog released on Wednesday . Delaying adjustments would lead to increasing interest burdens and fiscal vulnerabilities, further narrowing policy options. Financing conditions for many emerging market and developing economies had remained favorable, but might not last, the IMF said, urging those countries to also reduce their fiscal vulnerabilities and strengthen debt management. Low-income countries, where external financing was already tighter, needed to strengthen their tax systems and improve spending efficiency, the IMF said. High oil prices, persistent inflation, stronger investment demand and higher-than-expected AI growth have driven sharp increases in long-term sovereign yields in recent months. The Group of Seven's average 10-year government bond yield rose over 110 basis points between February and September, reaching its highest level in nearly two decades, the IMF said. The IMF said the effective average cost of government financing was projected to rise to 3.7% by 2031 from 2.3% in 2021. In the US, interest payments were expected to reach 5.3% of GDP, up from 2.8% of GDP before the COVID pandemic, roughly equal to its projected expenditure on Social Security. That number was even higher in low-income countries, where interest payments today consume over 15% of tax revenues, compared to an average cost of around 9% between 2011 and 2019. Adding to the stress, governments in advanced economies were refinancing more debt at shorter maturities, causing higher rates to pass through to government costs more quickly, the IMF said. For the G7 and Spain, it said, the share of debt maturing within one year was now approaching 30%. Inflation rates above target and higher energy prices meant central bankers would likely need to keep rates higher for longer, which in turn would limit governments' ability to respond to downturns, just as demands for increased spending on defense, energy security and aging populations were mounting. The IMF said interest rates on debt also now exceeded expected nominal growth rates in a number of countries, which would make it even harder for them to stabilize debt. Valdes said more countries were allowing higher energy prices to pass through, but many were still relying on costly, broad-based measures to shield their populations. "Our estimate is that taken together, the fiscal cost of all these measures is about one half percent of global GDP (gross domestic product)," he said, noting that a continuation of such measures would drive prices higher at the global level.

item.title: Nord Stream may have been lawful target, argue lawyers for Ukrainian accused of bombing
item.description: Lawyers for a Ukrainian ex-military officer accused of leading the bombing of Russia's Nord Stream pipeline in September 2022 argued at the start of his trial in Germany on Wednesday that "an aggressor's infrastructure" may have been a lawful target.
item.dc:creator: Miranda Murray
item.content:encoded: Lawyers for a Ukrainian ex-military officer accused of leading the bombing of Russia's Nord Stream pipeline in September 2022 argued at the start of his trial in Germany on Wednesday that "an aggressor's infrastructure" may have been a lawful target. Serhii Kuznetsov is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents including divers and an explosives expert that blew up Russia's largest gas pipeline to Europe in one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of modern times. The case provides the first opportunity for a public hearing of evidence gathered during a years-long investigation, which has been diplomatically and politically awkward for a German government that remains staunchly supportive of Ukraine despite the investigative trail linking Kyiv to the bombing. Moving to have the case dismissed, Kuznetsov's lawyer Nicola Canestrini argued that the pipeline — which provided half of Germany's imports of natural gas before Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine — was a "Russian weapon". "Is it unlawful to destroy an aggressor's infrastructure without harming any human beings?" Canestrini asked. RIGHT TO REMAIN SILENT Prosecutors have alleged that Kuznetsov, who was arrested under an international warrant in Italy last year, worked with members of the Ukrainian military to plan the [USN:L8N3UD0YM TEXT:"clandestine operation"] on behalf of unidentified Ukrainian state entities. Kuznetsov, 50, who prior to Wednesday was referred to publicly only as Serhii K. under German legal rules, has denied any involvement in the blasts that ruptured the 1,200-km (750-mile)-long Baltic Sea pipeline. Wearing a grey suit and with a shaved head, he exercised his right to remain silent in court but did not cover his face. His lawyers said he could not mount a proper defence because he was obliged to withhold Ukrainian state secrets. The government in Kyiv has also denied any involvement, a sensitive point in its relations with Germany, Ukraine's largest European supplier of military aid. Russia said on Monday it expected a "just verdict" that would reveal the names of the perpetrators and those who ordered the operation. Kuznetsov's legal team had tried reaching out to Ukraine for information that might assist the defence but heard nothing, according to another defence lawyer, Jes Meyer-Lohkamp. ATTACKING CIVILIAN TARGETS IS CONSIDERED A WAR CRIME German prosecutors say the actions Kuznetsov is accused of — attacking civilian targets and causing explosions that destroyed infrastructure and damaged public services — would amount to a war crime. Kuznetsov is the only person on trial, but Croatian authorities have [USN:L6N44H0T9 TEXT:"arrested"] another man, identified as Vladimir Z., who prosecutors believe was one of the [USN:SPN44900E TEXT:"divers"]. The explosion of Nord Stream sealed the end of Germany's longstanding dependence on Russian natural gas, although Moscow had already cut supplies over Berlin's support for European sanctions following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Nord Stream's supply had been due to double with the opening of a twin pipeline, Nord Stream 2, already built, but Berlin cancelled approval to open it just prior to Russia's invasion. PLUMES OF METHANE GAS The trial, expected to continue into February next year, could have domestic political implications. Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), leading in opinion polls for more than a year, has called for an end to military aid for Ukraine and a restoration of energy ties with Moscow. Although German state parliaments have no role in foreign policy, the AfD filed a motion in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt on Wednesday calling for an end to support for Ukraine, noting the "historical parallel" with the start of the trial. The Nord Stream system, lying at a depth of 80 to 110 metres under the Baltic and built by Russian gas concern Gazprom to supply up to 110 billion cubic metres of gas to Germany, was formerly at the core of economic ties between the two countries. The September 26, 2022 blasts that ruptured three of the four concrete-coated steel pipelines created a giant whirlpool at sea as huge plumes of methane gas rose into the atmosphere. Prosecutors allege that Kuznetsov travelled to Germany through Poland some three weeks before the attack, using a forged Ukrainian passport. He and his group then used a sailboat hired in the northern German city of Rostock to reach an area close to the Danish island of Bornholm, where they rigged specialised military-grade explosives to the sea floor. The weekly Der Spiegel magazine and ZDF public television have previously reported that five men and one woman were on the rented yacht Andromeda, which left Rostock on September 6 and returned on September 23, 2022.

item.title: 'Gift to our adversary': More Republicans criticize Trump's Russia diesel deal
item.description: A dozen US senators, including six Republicans, called on President Donald Trump on Tuesday to rescind his diesel deal with Russia, days before his administration must decide whether to formally impose new sanctions on Moscow over its war in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle, Valerie Volcovici
item.content:encoded: (This Oct 13 story has been corrected to clarify that Senator Chris Coons is from Delaware, not Connecticut, in paragraph 16.) A dozen US senators, including six Republicans, called on President Donald Trump on Tuesday to rescind his diesel deal with Russia , days before his administration must decide whether to formally impose new sanctions on Moscow over its war in Ukraine. The lawmakers' letter to Trump said the agreement provides Russian President Vladimir Putin's government with more fuel to finance its war , and will not benefit Americans, adding to a torrent of congressional criticism since Trump announced the deal on Friday. The resistance marks a shift from what had been Republicans' near-unanimous support for Trump's foreign policy decisions, weeks before November 3 midterm elections that will determine whether the party retains control of Congress. In his post, Trump said he was lifting sanctions on Russian diesel exports, and that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons (2.25 million barrels) of diesel to US and global markets. Although Trump said he wanted to reduce prices, the amount he referenced is less than a day's supply for the US transport sector alone, according to US Energy Information Administration data, which shows daily use of around 2.94 million barrels per day. "Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from Putin's murderous, illegal war," the lawmakers said in their letter. "This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies; it should be rescinded," they said. The senators' letter, dated Tuesday, was signed by Republicans Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, Thom Tillis of North Carolina, Susan Collins of Maine, Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and John Cornyn of Texas, as well as six Democrats. GRAHAM SANCTIONS BILL DEADLINE LOOMS Under [USN:L1N4570ZO TEXT:"a law"] Trump signed last month, he faces an October 18 deadline to impose sweeping new sanctions and tariffs on Russian energy over the Ukraine war, or waive them because he has determined that doing so is in the national interest. The letter urged Trump to execute the sanctions authorities included in the new law, called the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026", in honor of the late senator, a Russia hawk and close Trump ally who died in July. The administration has not yet told lawmakers whether it would impose the sanctions or issue a waiver. Collins, Murkowski and Tillis had joined Democrats in a [USN:O8N43T024 TEXT:"joint statement"] on Sunday calling on Trump to "reverse course" on [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"the deal"], saying it runs counter to US law barring imports of energy until Russia ends its aggression against Ukraine. Earlier on Tuesday, the Republican president [USN:S0N435010 TEXT:"was asked"] whether anyone had told him Russia could use proceeds of the diesel deal to purchase more bombs. "No, nobody told me anything," Trump responded, adding the deal benefited not just the US but the world. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak [USN:S8N45E0D7 TEXT:"said on Monday"] that Russia will be able to return diesel exports to levels above those Trump had outlined under the deal. The Democratic senators who signed the letter were Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Richard Durbin of Illinois, Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, Jack Reed of Rhode Island and Chris Coons of Delaware.

item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: Wall Street ouvre en baisse, le niveau de l'inflation américaine inquiète
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ouvre en baisse, le niveau de l'inflation américaine inquiète PARIS, 14 octobre (Reuters) - La Bourse de New York a ouvert en baisse mercredi après la publication d'un indicateur d'inflation aux Etats-Unis plus élevé que prévu, qui renforce les anticipations d'une hausse des taux directeurs ce mois-ci. La pénurie de diesel pourrait se prolonger jusqu'en 2027 selon l'AIE LONDRES, 14 octobre (Reuters) - Les tensions sur l'approvisionnement en diesel pourraient persister jusqu'en 2027 en raison d'importantes réductions de stocks, contraires à la tendance saisonnière, qui se sont combinées à une production restreinte à l'approche du pic de demande hivernal, déclare l'Agence internationale de l'énergie (AIE) dans son rapport mensuel sur le marché pétrolier. Le Portugal choisit Lufthansa, et non Air France-KLM, pour prendre 44,9% de TAP LISBONNE, 14 octobre (Reuters) - Le gouvernement portugais a annoncé mercredi avoir choisi Lufthansa pour acquérir une participation de 44,9% dans la compagnie TAP Air Portugal, pour 1,2 milliard d'euros, Lisbonne préférant ainsi la compagnie allemande à Air France-KLM, qui avait également soumis une offre. États-Unis: Les prix à la consommation progressent en septembre, tirés par le carburant 14 octobre (Reuters) - L'inflation aux États-Unis a accéléré en septembre, en raison notamment de la hausse des prix des carburants, montrent les données officielles publiées mercredi. BlackRock: Le bénéfice bondit au 3e trimestre, la bonne tenue des marchés fait grimper les commissions 14 octobre (Reuters) - BlackRock a annoncé mercredi une forte hausse de son bénéfice au troisième trimestre, le plus grand gestionnaire d'actifs au monde ayant perçu des commissions plus élevées grâce à la gestion des fonds de ses clients. Morgan Stanley: Bénéfice en hausse au 3e trimestre, porté par les opérations sur actions 14 octobre (Reuters) - Morgan Stanley a dépassé mercredi les prévisions de bénéfice pour le troisième trimestre, citant la hausse des revenus de la banque d'investissement et la bonne tenue des opérations sur actions, dans un contexte de volatilité dû à la décision de la Réserve fédérale américaine sur les taux d’intérêt et au conflit au Moyen-Orient BofA: Le bénéfice pénalisé par une amende de 1,2 milliard de dollars au 3e trimestre 14 octobre (Reuters) - Bank of America a affiché mercredi un bénéfice en recul au troisième trimestre, en raison de provisions de 1,2 milliard de dollars (1,07 milliards d'euros) pour couvrir les amendes infligées à la suite de défaillances dans la détection de cas potentiels de blanchiment d'argent et activités illicites. FMI-Washington doit réduire son déficit et la Chine augmenter sa consommation intérieure BANGKOK, 14 octobre (Reuters) - Les États-Unis ne peuvent sortir de la spirale de l'endettement avec la seule croissance économique, Washington n'ayant pas d'autre choix que de procéder à des ajustements fiscaux ou budgétaires, a déclaré mercredi la directrice générale du Fonds monétaire international (FMI), Kristalina Georgieva. L'UE cherche à se rapprocher du Vietnam pour se fournir en minerais et se détourner de la Chine HANOÏ, 14 octobre (Reuters) - L'Union européenne cherche à s'approvisionner davantage en minéraux stratégiques auprès du Vietnam afin de réduire sa dépendance vis-à-vis de la Chine, selon des documents internes de l'UE consultés par Reuters. L'accord diesel entre Washington et Moscou est un "choix très risqué" selon Meloni ROME, 14 octobre (Reuters) - L'accord conclu entre Washington et Moscou concernant l'approvisionnement en diesel est un "choix très risqué", sapant les efforts visant à contraindre le président russe Vladimir Poutine à cesser sa guerre contre l'Ukraine, a déclaré mercredi la présidente du Conseil italien Giorgia Meloni.

item.title: OFRTP Summary
item.description: Mélenchon présente un programme budgétaire censé réduire la dette de 25 milliards d'euros
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mélenchon présente un programme budgétaire censé réduire la dette de 25 milliards d'euros PARIS, 14 octobre (Reuters) - Le candidat de La France insoumise (LFI) à l'élection présidentielle, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, a présenté mercredi une feuille de route budgétaire prévoyant plus de 106 milliards d'euros de recettes, 82 milliards de dépenses et une réduction de la dette publique de 25 milliards. Le ministre polonais des Affaires étrangères demande à Musk s'il se livre à des manœuvres politiques avec Starlink en Ukraine VARSOVIE, 14 octobre (Reuters) - Le ministre polonais des Affaires étrangères Radosław Sikorski a demandé mercredi à Elon Musk s’il "faisait de la politique" avec Starlink en Ukraine, après que Kiev eut déclaré que SpaceX avait imposé une limitation sur certains services, perturbant ainsi les missions des drones de combat. Le pape Léon XIV a passé une nuit paisible après son opération selon le Vatican CITÉ DU VATICAN, 14 octobre (Reuters) - - Le pape Léon XIV a passé une nuit paisible à l'hôpital après son intervention chirurgicale lors de laquelle le lobe inférieur de son poumon droit a été retiré, a rapporté mercredi le Vatican. Pour Lagarde (BCE), la solution aux problèmes d'endettement de la France se trouve au niveau national BANGKOK, 14 octobre (Reuters) - La France devrait résoudre ses propres difficultés sur le marché obligataire par le biais de la politique budgétaire, a déclaré mercredi la présidente de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE), Christine Lagarde, minimisant ainsi les spéculations concernant une intervention de la BCE. Le parquet antiterroriste se saisit de l'enquête sur les tirs au collège d'Aubagne PARIS, 13 octobre (Reuters) - Le parquet national antiterroriste a annoncé mardi se saisir de l'enquête sur l'intrusion armée au collège Joseph-Lakanal d'Aubagne (Bouches-du-Rhône) d'un élève de l'établissement qui a ouvert le feu au fusil de chasse sur le proviseur et une enseignante, les blessant légèrement. La Russie condamne la saisie par la France d'un pétrolier au large de la Réunion L'ambassade de Russie à Paris a condamné mardi la saisie par la France du navire pétrolier DF Peak à 450 milles nautiques au large de la Réunion, annoncée la veille par Emmanuel Macron, la qualifiant d'acte de piraterie et de violation du droit international. Raphaël Glucksmann remporte la primaire social-démocrate dès le premier tour Le candidat Place Publique à l'élection présidentielle, Raphaël Glucksmann, a remporté dès le premier tour la primaire social-démocrate, a annoncé dimanche le Parti socialiste. La France appelle les autorités palestiniennes à revenir sur le report les élections La France regrette le report par le président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas des élections législatives et présidentielle, a déclaré dimanche un porte-parole du ministère des Affaires étrangères, appelant les autorités palestiniennes à revenir sur cette décision. Nobel/Littérature: Le prix décerné à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson Le prix Nobel de littérature a été décerné jeudi à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson pour "son oeuvre audacieuse et inventive qui, dans un dialogue ludique avec la tradition classique, a créé de nouvelles formes pour la littérature contemporaine", a annoncé jeudi l'Académie royale des sciences de Suède. Les deux Renoir dérobés au musée de Cagnes-sur-Mer retrouvés Les deux tableaux dérobés il y a un peu plus d'un mois au musée Renoir de Cagnes-sur-Mer (Alpes-Maritimes) ont été retrouvés par la police et six suspects ont été arrêtés, a déclaré vendredi le maire Rassemblement national (RN) de la ville, Bryan Masson.
